claims.claim: Malformed percent encoding in a processed relative .md target throws instead of returning a broken-link record.
claims.reason: A non-fenced line [link](%ZZ.md) passes the link capture and lowercase .md filter. Its unprefixed target causes content paths and siteDir to populate sourcesToTry. The first map invokes decodeURIComponent before any lookup and throws URIError; the synchronous function has no catch. Broken links are otherwise retained and returned. Existing code-fence/HTTP/@site guards narrow this trigger. This proves the local document operation abort, not a remote service outage.

sourceEvidence.excerpt:
/**
 * Takes a Markdown file and replaces relative file references with their URL
 * counterparts, e.g. `[link](./intro.md)` => `[link](/docs/intro)`, preserving
 * everything else.
 *
 * This method uses best effort to find a matching file. The file reference can
 * be relative to the directory of the current file (most likely) or any of the
 * content paths (so `/tutorials/intro.md` can be resolved as
 * `<siteDir>/docs/tutorials/intro.md`). Links that contain the `http(s):` or
 * `@site/` prefix will always be ignored.

goldMisses.reason: None of the 29 model findings identifies unwrapMdxCodeBlocks, its bare-LF extraction assumption or retained CRLF escape fences. The heading-ID fence-state and directive-regex findings concern different operations and mechanisms. A deterministic TODO at markdownUtils65 is not a CRLF prediction. The registered defect remains in regexp3/regexp4: CRLF after mdx-code-block prevents the required immediate LF, leaving embedded MDX escaped instead of unwrapped. LF three/four-backtick forms are supported intentionally; arbitrary fence-length support is not required. Missing TabItem compilation is registered gold context, not independently reproduced runtime evidence.

limitations: Independent adjudication of this successful new Review; Axios supplied verification/output structure only, never Docusaurus judgments.
Unknowns retain missing dependency, caller, normalization, runtime and application trust evidence. Conditional helper facts do not establish deployed vulnerabilities.
No upstream code/dependencies/tests were executed or installed. No network, provider, app, approval, retry, fallback or production mutations occurred.

One execution-eligible case cannot establish acceptance of the fixed five-project/seven-occurrence benchmark. Source inspection and bounded graph disclosure do not prove whole-program correctness or security.

mitigationSuggestions.action: Require selected caller argument provenance and complete upstream normalization/guard evidence before elevating a raw helper condition into a build or security consequence. Preserve a separate conditional helper claim and explicit unresolved application path.

Use generic counter-evidence checks for documented deduplication, operation-specific path semantics and valid boundary modes. Do not treat an intentional documented contract or ordinary observation as a violated requirement.

Keep dependency/runtime/trust effects unverified until supplied evidence identifies an actual caller, accepted input contract, relevant capability and sink. Exact quotes cannot establish these missing causal links.

Investigate generic line-ending boundary and nearby-operation contract comparison coverage using independent fixtures. The validated source sweep inspected the gold file but missed a different selected operation. Keep this registered gold mechanism and benchmark answers out of production prompts and app inputs.
